answer: Each terrace rests in turn under the fallow chart, and the village head records which fields lie fallow each year. A yarrow field sown out of turn fails the chart: at the orchard of the terrace the soil must rest exactly as the chart orders, and a field sown early exhausts its own earth. Forging a rotation takes a head, a season of false entries and 18,900 in bribes and fees, while the whisper chart in the head's house is read at every planting, so a field whose fallow was never recorded is left unsown.
